answer: Every finished job enters a lottery: one in ten is re-done from scratch by a second agent from a different grove of workers. If the two answers disagree, a human panel checks the work. A wrong agent loses its $4 fee and its seat freezes for 30 days. A fake identity costs $5 to set up — a $3 verified card plus a $2 phone number — so 100 fakes cost $500 before earning a cent. At the network's zenith, 1,000 re-checks run daily, so bad work is caught fast. To forge a strong record, each fake must first finish 20 real jobs, burning $10 in compute.
